newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan to sell controlling stake in Shanghai store.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan to sell controlling stake in Shanghai store.

text.p: Shanghai-based Japanese retailer Yaohan group plans to sell 15 percent of its 55-percent stake in a Shanghai department store to its Chinese partner, Japanese media reports said on Saturday.
Much of the proceeds from the deal will be used to finance debt repayment of the financially troubled Yaohan Japan Corp, which operates a supermarket chain in Japan, the reports said.

The Yaohan group in 1995 opened Nextage Shanghai, a department store billed as the world's largest with a floor space of some 110,000 square metres, as a joint venture with Shanghai No. 1 Department Store, which holds the other 45-percent stake.
Yaohan International Holdings Ltd, the group's holding company for Chinese operations, including Yaohan Hong Kong Corp, holds 36 percent of Nextage Shanghai. Yaohan Japan holds 19 percent.
The group is considering selling part of Yaohan Holdings' stake in Nextage Shanghai to Shanghai No. 1 Department Store for several billion yen, Kyodo news agency reported.
As a result of the sale, Shanghai No. 1 would gain a controlling stake in the venture and Yaohan would effectively relinquish its control on the business, the Nihon Keizai said.

Mitsumasa Wada, president of Yaohan Japan, was quoted by Kyodo as saying: "The group is considering selling its Nextage shares to the Chinese partner as part of restructuring measures. The Chinese side will beef up Nextage's sluggish business by localising its management."
Yaohan officials were not available to comment on the reports.
